rationale: Greek μετάγγισμος (μετα-+ἀγγεῖον 'vessel') = 'pouring from vessel to vessel.' Manichaean technical term distinct from μεταλλαγμός 'exchange' (already in glossary as ⲙⲉⲧⲁⲗⲗⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ). Designates the specific cosmic process by which Light-substance is decanted through successive material vessels (the metangismos = the metempsychotic vehicle of the Living Soul through plant/animal/human bodies). 'Transmutation' preserves the change-of-substance register; 'transmigration' captures the vessel-to-vessel transit. The chapter heading at line 32 marks this as the subject of the next kephalaion.

Greek ἐγκρατής 'self-controlled, continent.' Ascetic-technical term for the disciplined faithful. In this kephalaion functions as a multi-register cosmological title applied (1) to the captive Light extracted from Darkness, (2) to the metangismos-remainder, (3) to the New Man, (4) to the celibate, (5) to the man-after-marriage who renounces. 'Continent one' preserves the active-restraint sense over 'ascetic' or 'celibate.'

Confirmed in this passage's antithetical pairing with ⲡⲣⲙ̄ⲛⲃ̄ⲣⲣⲉ 'the New Man' (line 19). Same lexeme as cosmic 'Ancient One' in earlier glossary, here in Pauline anthropological register (παλαιὸς ἄνθρωπος, Romans 6:6) — the unredeemed flesh-self stripped off in conversion. Already noted in glossary; this attestation reaffirms.
